extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for novelists on creating deeply immersive settings that transport readers, applicable to both historical and contemporary fiction. Covers detail selection, sensory description, research methods (in-person and remote), and how to make setting function like a character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft an atmospheric setting / world building
rubrics_metrics.description: Creating an atmospheric setting—world building, if you will—is key to a deeply immersive reading experience. We recreate that moment in time, whether it’s 1889 Paris or 1942 in Siberia, deftly layering in details to make the reader feel as though they got hold of Doc Brown’s DeLorean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The setting should transport the reader; treat it intentionally and layer details to evoke a specific time and place rather than relying on generic descriptors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use brief era-specific daily-life details to signal time/place
rubrics_metrics.description: Short descriptions of items in daily life that are different from the present day—connecting a call through an operator, for example—help transport the reader to the appropriate era in the space of a few words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pick small, telling details (objects, routines, technologies) that quickly orient readers without long exposition; use concrete examples tied to everyday life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be diligent about cultural and logistical details
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether historical or contemporary, a sensory-rich novel requires the deft use of cultural details. An author shouldn’t bog the reader down with long descriptions of how the school system in Provence works, but a quick mention of how teachers are assigned at the national level and with only minimal regard for the preferences of the teacher candidates or the schools can be fascinating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research cultural practices and institutional logistics (e.g., education, medical systems, moving logistics) and use those facts to add dimension; pick details that illuminate character and plot rather than overwhelm the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research contemporary settings as thoroughly as historical ones
rubrics_metrics.description: Research is still very much a part of the equation for contemporary works. Taking time to study the logistics of moving to a foreign country, learning how the medical system works, or yes, even studying the history of the region, will add dimension to a setting if you use that knowledge carefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do targeted research on practical realities relevant to your story; integrate what you learn sparingly and purposefully so it serves the scene or character development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'info dump'—sprinkle details with a light hand
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid is the dreaded 'info dump,' sprinkle details with a light hand and save the interesting trivia that doesn’t serve the story for social media and other purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer small, organic insertions of world-detail within action and dialogue; remove or relocate interesting but nonessential exposition that slows pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write to all the senses (especially smell and taste)
rubrics_metrics.description: We writers often focus on the visual experience, and to a lesser degree the audio. ... describing touch, taste, and especially smell can add a powerfully evocative layer to the narrative. Smell is so closely tied to memory in the human brain that even a brief description of a scent can deliver a huge visceral response in the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly include touch, taste, and smell cues—e.g., food flavors and textures—to create visceral reader responses and primal connections to setting; use sensory details to deepen emotional resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel to the story’s location when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Traveling to the area where the story takes place is a powerful, if expensive, tool to add depth to a story. ... it gave me a better sense of the atmosphere in villages that I hadn’t visited in twenty years or more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On-location research yields impressions of atmosphere and spatial relationships that enrich description; if possible, combine trips to benefit multiple projects (promotional photos, archive visits, idea gathering) to maximize value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'armchair travel' and online tools when you can't go in person
rubrics_metrics.description: If you can’t hop on the next Air France flight, spend some time immersing yourself from the comfort of your own home. Fortunately, there are powerful online tools to help bring any contemporary real-life setting to life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use street-view maps, videos to capture sounds and spatial relationships, and news/opinion pieces about local cultural trends (e.g., France’s 'empty diagonal') to approximate on-the-ground knowledge and atmosphere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the setting function as a character
rubrics_metrics.description: The setting in The Memory of Lavender and Sage is as crucial as any character in the book, crafted with that intention: to breathe the Mistral winds of Provence onto the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intentionally develop setting’s presence and influence on mood and plot; use recurring sensory motifs and specific landscape/weather details to give setting agency and emotional weight.
